name: Youth Empowerment Fund (YEF) Grants
org: Urban Services YMCA, YMCA of Greater San Francisco (funded by SF DCYF)
city: San Francisco, CA (Urban Services YMCA, 1530 Buchanan St.)
what_you_do: You plan a youth-led project to help your San Francisco community or start a business, then apply for a grant. Picked projects can get up to $10,000, and you run the project and report on spending.
who_can_apply: Young people in San Francisco: teens 13 to 18 and young adults 18 to 24. Each project needs an Adult Ally, who is a mentor. It also needs a Fiscal Sponsor. That is a group that pays project costs, and YEF pays it back.
pay_detail: Not a paid job. Grants pay for your project: up to $10,000 per round, or $500 to $2,000 for a mini grant.
duration: Spring 2027 grants: spending starts about March 1, 2027; the grant ends June 7, 2027.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 round closed Sept 21, 2026. Spring 2027 round: application releases in November 2026 (exact day not posted) and is due Monday, Jan 4, 2027. Interviews January to February 2027.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online grant form on the YEF page when the Spring 2027 round opens. You will have an interview. If you are picked, you go to a required meeting and turn in some forms.
notes: Grants can go to what youth need, projects that fix a problem in your area, or a new business. Teens also serve as YEF Community Funders. They decide which teen projects get grants. The page lists their schools but not how to join. In 2026, small grants of $500 to $2,000 ran July 17 to Aug 31, 2026. They were for supplies and first time projects only. Office hours at Urban Services YMCA are Monday and Wednesday, 1:00 to 4:00 p.m. Other days are by appointment only. Contact Amber Ly at aly@ymcasf.org.
